title: How do 16k vs. 32k condensed chart budgets and Chart-Only, 4-Layer KB, and Note-RAG pathways compare across Gemma 4 (E4B, 12B, 26B) in standalone wahs-engine?
summary: To measure how larger condensed chart budgets interact with clinical rule enrichment and targeted note retrieval on dense longitudinal charts, we benchmarked all 18 combinations of 2 condensed chart token budgets (16k vs. 32k), 3 standalone wahs-engine pathways — (1) Condensed Chart Only, (2) Condensation + 4-Layer Clinical KB + Tier-0 Overflow, and (3) Condensation + single-patient BM25 Note-RAG + 4-Layer KB — and 3 open-weight Google Gemma 4 models (E4B, 12B, 26B) running on an NVIDIA H200 (141 GB HBM3e) via Ollama on the UW CIRG cobalt GPU inference server. The 900-cell benchmark evaluated 50 clinical questions across two multi-clinic >16k-token patient records: Marcus Vance (cardio-oncology/immunotherapy polypharmacy expanding from 13.8k tokens at 16k budget to 32.7k tokens at 32k) and de-identified PhysioNet MIMIC-IV-on-FHIR ICU patient 10014354 (4,048 FHIR entries expanding from 13.0k to 23.6k tokens), graded blind by two independent frontier AI judges under strict-majority harm consensus alongside deterministic citation, atomic-entailment, abstention, and SDOH/IPV privacy guardrails.
takeaway: Tighter 16k chart condensation beat 32k across every Gemma 4 size and pathway, led by Gemma 4 26B + Condensation & Note-RAG (16k budget) at 83.6/100 (81.2 safety-adjusted; 8.84/10 accuracy, 8.12/10 completeness, 8.54/10 relevance; 2/50 confirmed unsafe + 2/50 disputed 1/2 judge splits, 0 unresolved chart references, 3.11s median p50 / 3.64s mean wait), followed by Gemma 4 26B + 4-Layer KB at 16k (81.2/100, 77.5 safety-adjusted, 2.42s median p50 / 2.70s mean), Gemma 4 26B + 4-Layer KB at 32k (80.6/100, 76.7 safety-adjusted, 2.80s median p50), Gemma 4 26B Chart-Only at 16k (80.2/100, 76.3 safety-adjusted, 2.08s median p50), and Gemma 4 12B Chart-Only at 16k (79.8/100, 75.8 safety-adjusted vs. 78.4 for 12B KB and 12B Note-RAG). Across all 9 arms per budget (450 cells each), 16k outperformed 32k on Benchmark /100 (78.7 vs. 75.4; safety-adjusted 75.0 vs. 71.3), accuracy (8.40 vs. 8.15), completeness (7.71 vs. 7.31), fewer disputed splits (19 vs. 29 alongside 29 vs. 30 confirmed unsafe), and median p50 speed (2.90s vs. 3.29s) — holding across 26B (81.7 vs. 78.9), 12B (78.9 vs. 75.6), and E4B (75.7 vs. 71.5; E4B Note-RAG dropped 75.1 -> 69.7). Cohort & pathway discrepancies: MIMIC-IV 10014354 improved slightly at 32k (79.3 -> 80.6) when moving up to clean folded history, whereas Marcus Vance dropped -8.0 pts (78.2 -> 70.1; disputed splits 7 -> 17) because pre-fix Tier 0 unfolding evicted recent vitals and his discharge summary; meanwhile 12B Chart-Only (16k) beat 12B KB and Note-RAG (79.8 vs. 78.4) because extra KB/note blocks led 12B to volunteer unasked medications without discharge hold caveats or invert historical dates. Strict-majority N=2 consensus separated 59/900 confirmed unsafe answers from 48/900 single-judge (1/2) disputed splits (0/900 third-party privacy breaches, 0 unresolved chart references across all 900 cells, 899/900 or 99.89% deterministic guardrail pass; Krippendorff's alpha: 0.726 accuracy, 0.764 completeness, 0.750 relevance, 0.772 abstention).
